items.title: A Drone Killed Three Ukrainians. It Was Guided Entirely by A.I.
items.summary: An attack by what Ukrainian officials said was a Russian drone with an Nvidia chip presages a dystopian future of weaponry untethered to humans.

items.title: Iran Cracks Down on One Luxury Left to Its Youth: Coffee Shops
items.summary: In recent weeks, the police have closed dozens of cafes, often citing laws that stipulate women must veil in public. Experts say the closures are part of an effort to control public space.

items.title: Can ‘Argentina’s Texas’ Save the Country’s Economy?
items.summary: Thousands of Argentines are flocking to a remote stretch of Patagonia, seeking work with only backpacks, tents and the hope that they and their country can turn around their fortunes.

items.title: As El Niño Dries Indonesia, Wildfires Intensify
items.summary: The unusual weather pattern and dried out peatlands, a kind of wetland, have been behind some of the country’s worst fire seasons. This year could be one.

items.title: UK Prime Minister Burnham Arrives in Ukraine as Russia Amps Up Warnings
items.summary: In his first foreign trip since taking office, the British prime minister pledged to stand by Kyiv despite new warnings of potential consequences.

items.title: Iran Pledges to Defy Trump’s Economic Sanctions
items.summary: Analysts say Tehran could intensify the dispute militarily after attempts to squeeze its economy. An Iranian official vowed “not a single drop of oil” would leave the Gulf.

items.title: Syria and Israel Hold U.S.-Mediated Talks to Try to Ease Tensions
items.summary: The discussions, reported by the Syrian state news agency, came days after Israel struck an air base in Syria’s northwest, the latest in a series of military interventions.

items.title: Some of Russia’s A.I. Drones Are Powered by Nvidia Microcomputers, Ukrainian Officials Say
items.summary: The tech giant says it does not sell the devices in Russia, but they are widely available on resale markets. When purchased that way, they are virtually impossible to track.

items.title: Man Who Told of a Childhood With Wolves Dies at 80
items.summary: Marcos Rodríguez Pantoja’s improbable story of a wild youth became the subject of a study, and inspired a novel and film.

items.title: A Chinese Robot Beat Usain Bolt’s 100-Meter Record. Should We Be Impressed?
items.summary: China’s humanoid robots are achieving superhuman feats of athleticism. But how that translates into the real world is still an open question, experts said.

items.title: S.E.C. Investigating Near-Implosion of A.I. Hedge Fund
items.summary: Regulators sent subpoenas to major Wall Street banks seeking information about the trading of Situational Awareness, three people briefed on the outreach said.

items.title: What’s Behind the U.S. Treasury’s Latest Attempt to Lower Interest Rates
items.summary: The Treasury Department said it could begin to buy back more of its debt, and bond market investors are assessing the potential effects on borrowing costs.

items.title: How Farmers Are Staying Afloat as Crop Prices Plunge
items.summary: Most U.S. farmers will lose money this year. Landowners and investors are increasingly trying to make money from their land, not what can be grown from it.

items.title: Trump Threatens New 50% Tariffs on Cars, Trucks and Steel as U.S.-Canada Trade War Unfolds
items.summary: President Trump vowed to increase tariffs on cars, trucks, auto parts and steel to 50 percent starting Jan. 1, as the countries edged toward a full-blown trade war.

items.title: Canada Is Retaliating Against Trump’s Tariffs. Will Others Follow?
items.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s decision to retaliate against U.S. tariffs has drawn praise from China, and exposed a rift in the Trump administration.

items.title: Research Firm’s Founder Explains $6 Million Payment to Fired Forbes Editor
items.summary: RJ Shook of Shook Research said he paid Randall Lane, the former top editor at Forbes, for “services and guidance” in partnering with Forbes and later selling his research firm.

items.title: Washington Post Ordered to Rehire Fired Columnist Karen Attiah
items.summary: An arbitrator ordered the newspaper to reinstate Karen Attiah, who was fired after posting about “white men who espouse hatred and violence” following Charlie Kirk’s killing.

items.title: Oil Prices Fall Ahead of U.S. Vow to Intensify Economic War Against Iran
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is expected to announce an escalation of sanctions aimed at further isolating Iranian trade.

items.title: Los Angeles Dodgers Owner’s Troubles Roil Insurance World
items.summary: Federal investigations of Mark Walter’s business empire have put a spotlight on private-equity-owned insurers that invest premiums in risky assets.

items.title: Netflix, YouTube and Amazon Want You to Watch Everything From One App: Theirs
items.summary: YouTube is racing to catch up to Amazon, which already offers users the chance to subscribe to services like HBO Max from within its app. Netflix is increasingly open to the idea, too.

items.title: After Hugging Face Was Attacked By A.I. Agents, It Embarked on a Crusade
items.summary: Hugging Face, a start-up that was breached by rogue bots from OpenAI, is using the hack to push for openness in A.I. development.

items.title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
items.summary: Companies like Google and Microsoft have used their money, their might and their massive reach to influence nearly every step of the education supply chain.

items.title: The Data Center Backlash Bursts Into the Midterms
items.summary: With opposition to the centers mounting, many Democrats and a growing number of Republicans are campaigning against them.

items.title: The U.S. Start-Up Making Low-Cost Interceptors for the Iran War
items.summary: For Florida-based Powerus, becoming a global supplier of counterdrone technology has meant involving the Trumps, a golf course and a new way of doing business.

items.title: Laptop Fire on American Airlines Flight Injures at Least One Passenger
items.summary: Flight attendants used a fireproof bag to contain the computer after its lithium battery began smoking. One passenger was treated on the ground for injuries.

items.title: Four Years Ago, a Crypto Boss Went Missing. Now His Successor Has.
items.summary: The mysterious collapse of a European cryptocurrency exchange helps to explain why the industry hasn’t shaken off its reputation as a magnet for criminals.

items.title: What if Your Texts Traveled as Slowly as a Carrier Pigeon?
items.summary: Apps that let users send digital messages at ultraslow speeds have taken off, with users reveling in a slower pace of life. (Just don’t use the them to make dinner plans.)

items.title: Anthropic Could Aim to Raise $100 Billion in Blockbuster I.P.O.
items.summary: The offering could value the five-year-old A.I. start-up at $2 trillion, its bankers have told potential investors, which would exceed Elon Musk’s SpaceX.

items.title: TikTok Settles With U.S. Over Child Privacy Concerns for $400 Million
items.summary: The Justice Department resolved a lawsuit that accused the social media company of illegally gathering children’s information.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Buys an Irish Castle
items.summary: The prominent landowner has added a nearly 200-year-old estate to his holdings. Archival information says it can take “a brisk walk of 4½ minutes to reach the dining room from the kitchen.”
